implement.summary: Gap on BASE_SHA 7cfeacbb (VERIFIED): the Edge router in supabase/functions/api/index.ts had no `POST /v1/offline/receipts` case (the offline family ended at grant issuance/refresh/release — `case "POST /v1/offline/grants"` and the ticket RPCs consume_offline_ticket/release_offline_ticket from 20260908160000_offline_device_grants.sql), so a device that rated offline had no way to report consumption later; there was no durable receipt identity anywhere in supabase/migrations (no table keyed by receipt id/digest), so nothing could make a redelivered or reordered batch idempotent, and nothing recorded a HOLD for ambiguous evidence. packages/shared-types already defined OfflineResultReceipt / OfflineReconciliationStatus (reconciliation_required with reserved|not_applicable dispositions) and the canonical-JSON digest helpers, but no server code consumed them. Fix: (1) migration 20260909220000_offline_receipt_settlement.sql adds public.offline_receipt_settlements — one row per (user_id, receipt_id) carrying receipt_sha256 and the owner/installation/grant/grant-jws-digest/allocation/generation/ticket/operation/result/output-digest/billing bindings plus the verdict; RLS on, ALL grants revoked from public/anon/authenticated/service_role (RPC is the only reader/writer), append-only trigger that permits DELETE only via the account cascade; settle_offline_receipt(p_receipt, p_receipt_sha256, p_output, p_hold_reason) SECURITY DEFINER, EXECUTE only to authenticated, requires auth.uid() + is_api_session_active(), takes access_lock_key(uid) and the ticket lock, then: same (receipt_id, digest) → replay the stored verdict; same receipt_id/other digest → offline.receipt_conflict; Edge hold reason / owner mismatch / already-recorded operation or result / allocation mismatch / missing output → reconciliation_required with the ticket left reserved (financial_disposition reserved or not_applicable — never returned, never a new operation); otherwise chargeable tickets consume exactly once through the existing consume_offline_ticket() (consumed only on joint_verification_required results), not_chargeable and no-ticket receipts record the result without consuming. (2) index.ts wires `POST /v1/offline/receipts` (body {receipts:[{receipt,grant,output}]}, 1–25 entries, 2 MB cap) behind the normal authenticated dispatch (live-session check inherited), with its own per-user budget (25/min), per-entry shape validation via the shared-types validators (malformed entries rejected without a DB call), grant verification as the caller (verifyOfflineExecutionGrant with owner+installation binding, evaluated as of the grant's last live instant because delayed receipts legitimately arrive after exp), receipt→grant digest, grant jti, ticket ∈ allocation, output.id and canonical output digest checks — each failure becomes an explicit HOLD reason handed to the RPC, never a refund; every RPC/DB failure is a generic 503 via serviceUnavailable() with detail only in logs; one categorical audit line per batch. (3) security_regression.sql section U (U1–U5) pins all of it live and extends the RPC/table privilege inventories. (4) accountDeletionOperations.ts registers the table as cascade_only. Pushed to origin devin/pp/w04-04/impl-r1 only; no PR opened, nothing deployed, production project untouched.

blocking_issues: supabase/migrations/20260909220000_offline_receipt_settlement.sql:302-313 together with supabase/functions/api/index.ts:5183-5190 — a legitimately re-issued ticket can never settle. issue_offline_grant() (T2/T10 in security_regression.sql, and the reviewer probe) re-issues the SAME outstanding ticket ids under generation N+1 with a NEW grant id, and writes no new 'allocated' ledger row; the mobile wallet (apps/mobile/src/data/offlineCapabilities.ts:1041-1058) moves remaining tickets to the new grant_id/allocation_id/generation, so every receipt the device produces after a refresh names the generation-N+1 grant. index.ts:5185-5186 requires receipt.ticket.allocationId/generation == the presented grant's claims (the new grant), while the RPC requires the ledger's ORIGINAL allocated row to equal those same values (`v_allocation.grant_id <> v_grant_id or ... <> v_allocation_id or v_allocation.generation <> v_generation`). Both cannot hold at once, so the honest receipt is HELD as evidence_ambiguous with the ticket 'reserved' forever and the lifetime-free rating is stranded (never settled, never chargeable, no reconciliation route). REPRODUCE (disposable DB, all HEAD migrations): run reissue_probe.sql via `docker exec -i pickle-xc-pg psql -U postgres -d postgres -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 < reissue_probe.sql` — output: generation 1 allocates t1,t2; generation 2 returns the same ids; settle_offline_receipt() for the same ticket/output under the g2 grant → `accepted | held | reconciliation_required | evidence_ambiguous | reserved`, under the (superseded) g1 grant → `accepted | settled | consumed`. Probe + log: reissue_probe.sql / reissue_probe.log attachments. FIX: bind the ticket to its allocation LINEAGE, not the literal allocated row — accept when the receipt's grant is a grant of the same user/device whose issue restated this ticket (e.g. the grant row for v_grant_id exists for the ledger row's device with generation >= the allocated generation, or record a 'reissued' ledger event per generation and match against it), keep the existing HOLD for foreign grants/devices/installations, and add a live test (security_regression.sql section U + offline_receipt_reconciliation.test.ts) proving a receipt under generation 2 for a generation-1 ticket settles exactly once (and that its duplicate under generation 1 then replays/holds, not double-consumes). This is a correctness defect in the package objective ('bound to grant/ticket' must not misclassify honest evidence as ambiguous) and a billing-conservation problem (paid-for ratings never delivered, tickets never usable), not a security regression.

No security invariant is violated: new table has RLS on with ALL privileges revoked from public/anon/authenticated/service_role, RPC EXECUTE only to authenticated, RPC requires auth.uid() + api_private.is_active_session(), locks access_lock_key(uid) then the ticket lock, table is append-only (DELETE only via the profile cascade), route is behind the authenticated dispatch with its own 25/min per-user budget, DB/RPC failures answer generic 503, no grants widened, no applied migration edited, no existing comments edited (all 5 removed lines are code lines extended in place), no test weakened/reordered (http_test.ts 19→20 is a one-literal inventory acknowledgement of the one new audit sink).

breaks.expected: Per-receipt verdicts: an already-consumed receipt replays its durable verdict (result_recorded/consumed); a receipt bound to a different approved lineage is judged against THAT lineage; a receipt under a withdrawn lineage is a grant_revoked HOLD; a not_chargeable abstention is recorded. Withdrawal of the active release must never make already-consumed offline receipts unreportable (the device cannot reconcile them and the message 'No rating was counted' is false for a consumed ticket).
breaks.observed: HTTP 409 {"error":{"code":"access.release_not_authorized","message":"Validated ratings are not available right now. implement.approach: Started from BASE_SHA 7cfeacbb on a fresh branch devin/pp/w04-04/impl-r2; cherry-picked the sound r1 commits (route + migration + tests, ea9c6f0f/15bd43d2/6b3c0aa9), then committed the r2 regression tests FIRST (26a8c72d) and the fix last (b214adf5). Fix, all inside the package's paths: (1) settle_offline_receipt() binds a ticket to its allocation LINEAGE instead of literal allocated-row equality — the receipt's grant must be an `identity_lifetime_free` grant of the same user/installation (offline_grants ⋈ offline_devices) issued at/after the ticket's 'allocated' ledger row with the receipt's generation, and the caller must own the ticket via api_private.offline_ticket_owned_by() (original-owner recovery); foreign owner/grant/installation/ticket evidence still HOLDs reserved, and a Pro grant cannot claim a free-ticket lineage. (2) consume_offline_ticket() = 'shot.session_not_found' answers delivery='pending' (nothing durable, ticket reserved) instead of a permanent hold; the route reports `pending` in results/tallies. (3) generation/lifecycle_sequence are bigint bounded 1..9007199254740991 (JSON numeric checked) so 2147483648 gets a durable verdict. (4) New service_role-only RPC read_analysis_release_policy_lineage(p_policy_sha256) returns an installed (active or superseded) policy by digest; the route resolves the grant's `release.policy.sha256` against the active policy first, else the lineage (cached once per batch), verifies it with the existing release-policy verifier, admits under the grant's issue instant, maps withdrawn → grant_revoked hold, unknown/integrity → evidence_ambiguous hold, and storage/transport failures → generic 503 (never a durable decision on missing data). security_regression.sql U6–U9 pin all of it on the SQL plane across fresh + historical upgrade paths.
